name: Barcelona
intro: Gaudí's city by the sea: modernist houses, a medieval old town, a hill of gardens and a long city beach. Very walkable, with an easy metro.

transit.note: Metro runs roughly 5:00–24:00, later on Fridays and all night on Saturdays.

sources: Converted from the Barcelona 2026 family trip guide (coordinates OSM-verified)

areas.name: Sagrada Família & Sant Pau
areas.blurb: Gaudí's basilica and the tiled hospital town.

areas.name: Passeig de Gràcia
areas.blurb: Modernist houses on the city's grand avenue.

areas.name: Gothic Quarter & La Rambla
areas.blurb: Medieval lanes, Roman columns and the market.

areas.name: El Born & Ciutadella
areas.blurb: Picasso, Santa Maria del Mar and the big park.

areas.name: Port Vell & Barceloneta
areas.blurb: Harbour walk, fish market and the city beach.

areas.name: Port Olímpic & Poblenou
areas.blurb: Quieter beaches and a local rambla.

areas.name: Montjuïc
areas.blurb: Castle hill, gardens, museums and the Magic Fountain.

areas.name: Gràcia & Park Güell
areas.blurb: Gaudí's park and the village squares of Gràcia.

areas.name: El Carmel & Guinardó
areas.blurb: Hilltop viewpoints over the whole city.

areas.name: Sarrià & Tibidabo foothills
areas.blurb: CosmoCaixa science museum and quiet gardens.

pois.name: Sagrada Família
pois.why: Gaudí's basilica, under construction since 1882 and now the tallest church in the world. The stained-glass light inside is the highlight.
pois.kid: Find the two tortoises holding up columns on the Nativity façade: one land tortoise, one sea turtle.
pois.tip: 9:00–10:00 is the daily Quiet Hour: calmer, great for kids. Book only on sagradafamilia.org; resellers add €26–40.
inside: Nave: columns branch like a stone forest under the ceiling
Stained glass: cool blues and greens on the Nativity side in the morning, reds and oranges on the Passion side later
Altar with the hanging crucifix canopy, then the apse
Museum and Gaudí's crypt, included in the ticket
Towers (separate timed ticket, lift up, stairs down)

pois.name: Plaça de Gaudí
pois.why: The pond gives the classic reflection photo of the Nativity towers. Small playground.
pois.kid: Take the 'upside-down Sagrada' photo in the water.
pois.tip: Best light in the morning.
inside: Pond with the reflection of the Nativity towers
Best photo spot for the full façade

pois.name: Avinguda de Gaudí
pois.transitStop: Sagrada Família (L2, L5) or Sant Pau | Dos de Maig (L5)
pois.why: Car-free avenue linking Sagrada Família and Sant Pau, lined with modernist lampposts.
pois.kid: Look back halfway: both buildings line up at each end.
pois.tip: Café terraces here are pricey; buy snacks at a bakery on a side street.
inside: Car-free avenue with a view of Sagrada Família behind you and Sant Pau ahead
Modernist lampposts and benches along the whole length
Bakeries and cafés in the side streets

pois.name: Sant Pau Recinte Modernista
pois.transitStop: Sant Pau | Dos de Maig (L5), 3 min
pois.why: A hospital built like a fairy-tale town with tiled domes by Domènech i Montaner.
pois.kid: Count the colours on the tiled roofs.
pois.tip: The street view is good enough if you're saving money.
inside: Tiled domes and the main façade, seen from the entrance
Pavilions linked by underground tunnels (inside visit)
Domènech i Montaner's mosaics and stained glass

pois.name: Honest Greens
pois.transitStop: Passeig de Gràcia (L2, L3, L4); choose the branch nearest to you on Maps
pois.why: Counter-service grain-and-protein bowls near Passeig de Gràcia. Quick and filling.
pois.kid: Simple plates with chicken, rice or potatoes.
pois.tip: Several branches in Eixample; tap Maps for the nearest one.
inside: Build-your-own bowls with grains, greens and grilled chicken or fish

pois.name: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
pois.why: Gaudí's wavy stone apartment block. No straight walls on the façade.
pois.kid: The rooftop chimneys look like knights' helmets. Spot them from the street corner.
pois.tip: Price changes by demand; outside views are free.
inside: Wavy stone façade with seaweed-shaped iron balconies (from the street)
Rooftop with warrior-shaped chimneys and city views (inside)
Attic with brick catenary arches and a Gaudí exhibition (inside)

pois.name: Casa Batlló
pois.transitStop: Passeig de Gràcia (L2, L3, L4), 3 min
pois.why: The 'house of bones': balconies like masks and a roof shaped like a dragon's back.
pois.kid: Find the dragon's spine on the roof and the knight's lance (the cross tower).
pois.tip: Inside visit is kid-friendly but optional on a budget day.
inside: Façade of tile mosaic and skull-shaped balconies
Noble floor with swirling ceilings and oak doors (inside)
Blue-tiled light well, darker tiles at the top (inside)
Roof terrace with the dragon-back roof (inside)

pois.name: Casa Amatller
pois.transitStop: Passeig de Gràcia (L2, L3, L4), 3 min
pois.why: Next door to Casa Batlló. Three architects competed side by side on this 'Block of Discord'.
pois.kid: Spot the stepped gable that looks like a gingerbread house.
pois.tip: Chocolate shop on the ground floor (the Amatllers made chocolate).
inside: Chocolate shop and café on the ground floor

pois.name: Plaça de Catalunya
pois.why: The city's central square and main metro hub. End of the day's walk.
pois.kid: Fountains and sculptures around the square.
pois.tip: Main metro hub: lines L1 and L3.
inside: Start of La Rambla and Portal de l'Àngel shopping street
Largest metro and train hub in the city

pois.name: Casa de les Punxes
pois.why: A brick 'castle' with six pointed towers in the middle of the Eixample grid.
pois.kid: Does it look like a fairy-tale castle or a witch's house?
pois.tip: 5 min walk from Casa Milà along Diagonal.
inside: Six pointed towers on a brick façade

pois.name: Jardins de la Torre de les Aigües
pois.why: A hidden courtyard garden inside an Eixample block, with an old water tower. Enter through a doorway on Carrer de Roger de Llúria 56.
pois.kid: A secret garden behind a normal-looking door.
pois.tip: Opening hours vary out of summer; peek in when passing.

pois.name: Passatge Permanyer
pois.transitStop: Passeig de Gràcia (L2, L3, L4), 4 min
pois.why: A quiet lane of small townhouses with front gardens, unusual in the Eixample.
pois.kid: Pick your favourite little house.
pois.tip: Gates may be closed at times; look through from the street.
inside: Lane of 19th-century townhouses with small front gardens

pois.name: Parc de l'Estació del Nord
pois.transitStop: Marina (L1) or Arc de Triomf (L1), 10 min
pois.why: Open park with Beverly Pepper's blue-tiled land sculptures you can walk over.
pois.kid: Run along the blue tile waves like a dragon's tail.
pois.tip: Next to the bus station, 15 min from Sagrada Família.

pois.name: La Rambla
pois.transitStop: Catalunya (L1, L3) at the top, Liceu (L3) in the middle, Drassanes (L3) at the bottom
pois.why: The famous promenade. Walk it once, downhill, and keep going.
pois.kid: Find Joan Miró's colourful mosaic set into the pavement.
pois.tip: Busiest pickpocket zone in the city. Bags zipped and in front. Don't eat here.
inside: Walk downhill from Plaça de Catalunya to the harbour
Canaletes fountain and the Liceu opera house
Joan Miró's round mosaic in the pavement by the Boqueria
Flower stalls and kiosks along the central strip

pois.name: La Boqueria market
pois.why: Covered market with fruit pyramids, jamón and sweets.
pois.kid: Pick a fresh juice colour each.
pois.tip: Stalls deeper inside are cheaper than at the entrance. Open Mon–Sat.
inside: Fruit and juice stalls at the front (tourist prices)
Fish and seafood in the centre
Jamón, cheese and nuts in the back aisles
Counter bars for a quick sit-down breakfast

pois.name: Plaça Reial
pois.why: Palm-tree square with arcades.
pois.kid: The lampposts were Gaudí's very first job for the city.
pois.tip: Toilets: use a café you buy something in.
inside: Gaudí's lampposts, his first public commission

pois.name: Barcelona Cathedral
pois.why: Gothic cathedral with a huge front square.
pois.kid: 13 white geese live in the cloister, one for each year of young Saint Eulàlia's life.
pois.tip: Shoulders and knees covered to enter.
inside: Gothic façade and the front square
Choir stalls and the Christ of Lepanto chapel
Cloister garden with its white geese and fountain

pois.name: Plaça de Sant Felip Neri
pois.why: A tiny, quiet square with a sad story.
pois.kid: The holes in the church wall come from a 1938 bombing.
pois.tip: Speak softly; there's a school here.
inside: Small quiet square with a fountain
Shrapnel marks on the church wall from the 1938 bombing

pois.name: Pont del Bisbe
pois.why: The lacy stone bridge everyone photographs.
pois.kid: Legend says a skull with a dagger is hidden under the bridge. Can you find it?
pois.tip: Stand on Carrer del Bisbe for the classic shot.
inside: Neo-Gothic bridge (1928) between two government buildings
Look up from Carrer del Bisbe for the classic view
Generalitat palace façade next to it

pois.name: Conesa Entrepans
pois.why: Toasted sandwiches since 1951 with 90+ fillings, on Plaça Sant Jaume.
pois.kid: Ham-and-cheese toastie is a safe pick.
pois.tip: Order at the counter, eat on the square.
inside: Order at the counter, eat outside or take away

pois.name: Temple d'August
pois.why: Four 2,000-year-old Roman columns hidden inside a courtyard.
pois.kid: These columns are older than the city's name. It was called Barcino.
pois.tip: Small site; may have short opening hours. Peek in if open.
inside: Inside the courtyard of the Centre Excursionista de Catalunya (Carrer Paradís 10)

pois.name: Plaça del Rei
pois.why: The medieval royal square. Under it lie Roman streets (MUHBA museum).
pois.kid: Pretend you're arriving at the king's palace up the stone steps.
pois.tip: MUHBA museum is a good rainy option.
inside: Medieval royal square with the Palau Reial Major
MUHBA museum under the square: Roman streets and laundry (paid)

pois.name: Santa Maria del Mar
pois.why: The 'cathedral of the sea', built by port workers who carried the stones.
pois.kid: Look for the carved porters with stones on their backs on the doors.
pois.tip: Sit on the steps for a break.
inside: Plain, tall Gothic interior with slender octagonal pillars
Carved porters (bastaixos) on the doors, who carried the stone

pois.name: El Born CCM
pois.costNote: Free entry to the ruins view
pois.why: An old iron market built over the streets of 1714 Barcelona. You look down on them.
pois.kid: Find the old houses' doorways down in the dig.
pois.tip: Closed on Mondays.
inside: Excavated streets and houses of 1714 under the market hall
Exhibition on the 1714 siege (some parts paid)

pois.name: La Pizza del Born
pois.why: Pizza by the slice on Passeig del Born. Cheap and quick.
pois.kid: Easy dinner for a tired walker.
pois.tip: Dinner in Spain starts late; slice shops suit families.
inside: Pizza by the slice on Passeig del Born

pois.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
pois.why: Concert hall with mosaic columns and flower tiles on the outside.
pois.kid: Find the mosaic pillars and the stone singers on the corner.
pois.tip: 5 min from the cathedral.

pois.name: Mercat de Santa Caterina
pois.why: Market with a wavy roof of over 300,000 tiles in fruit-and-vegetable colours.
pois.kid: From the side street, the roof looks like a wave of fruit.
pois.tip: Calmer and cheaper than La Boqueria.
inside: Fresh food stalls and small restaurants
Roman and medieval remains visible under the floor

pois.name: Roman walls, Plaça de Ramon Berenguer
pois.why: A long stretch of Roman city wall with towers, right on the street.
pois.kid: Roman soldiers once guarded these towers.
pois.tip: On Via Laietana, by Jaume I metro.
inside: Roman wall with towers from the 4th century
Stairs up to the Bishop's palace

pois.name: El Call (old Jewish quarter)
pois.why: The narrowest, twistiest lanes of the old town.
pois.kid: Can you touch both walls at once in the narrowest lane?
pois.tip: Between the cathedral and Plaça Sant Jaume.
inside: Narrowest lanes of the old Jewish quarter

pois.name: Carrer de Montcada
pois.why: Medieval street of merchant palaces with courtyards you can peek into.
pois.kid: Look up for stone faces on the walls.
pois.tip: The Picasso Museum is on this street.
inside: Medieval merchant palaces with open courtyards
Textile and Fashion museum in a palace

pois.name: Turó de les Tres Creus
pois.transitStop: Vallcarca (L3), then the outdoor escalators, about 15 min
pois.why: Hilltop with three crosses in Park Güell's free area: 360° view over the city and sea.
pois.kid: Climb to the top and find the Sagrada Família towers.
pois.tip: Get here first, before your timed slot.
inside: 360° view: Sagrada Família, the port, Tibidabo
Shaded paths on the way up

pois.name: Park Güell Monumental Zone
pois.transitStop: Vallcarca (L3) or Lesseps (L3), 15–20 min uphill; bus 24 stops at the Carretera del Carmel gate
pois.why: The mosaic salamander, the wavy bench terrace and the gingerbread gatehouses.
pois.kid: Count the columns in the Hypostyle Room (there are 86).
pois.tip: Book on parkguell.barcelona. Arrive no more than 30 min late or the ticket is void.
inside: Dragon (salamander) fountain on the entrance staircase
Hypostyle Room: 86 Doric columns with tiled medallions
Nature Square: the long curved bench in broken-tile mosaic

pois.name: Bunkers del Carmel
pois.transitStop: Bus 24 or V17 to the foot of the hill; check Maps for the nearest stop
pois.why: Old anti-aircraft base from 1937 on top of Turó de la Rovira. The widest view in Barcelona.
pois.kid: Spot the sea, Montjuïc and the Sagrada Família.
pois.tip: Gates close in the early evening (earlier in winter): check the sign at the bottom. Steep final climb, no toilets, bring water.
inside: 360° viewing platform on top of the old gun emplacements
Skyline: Sagrada Família, port, Montjuïc, Tibidabo
Grass and walls for watching the sunset

pois.name: Casa Vicens
pois.why: Gaudí's first house, covered in green-and-white tiles with marigold flowers.
pois.kid: Find the tiny painted flowers on the tiles.
pois.tip: Good rainy-day interior.
inside: Façade of green-and-white tiles with marigold flowers
Smoking room with a carved ceiling (inside)

pois.name: Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia
pois.why: Village square with a tall clock tower. Gràcia used to be its own town.
pois.kid: Local kids play football and ride scooters here.
pois.tip: Benches for a break.

pois.name: Plaça del Sol
pois.why: The liveliest square in Gràcia, full of families in the early evening.
pois.kid: Space to run around.
pois.tip: Ice cream shops nearby.
inside: Liveliest square in Gràcia, outdoor terraces
Local families in the early evening
Ice cream and bakeries on nearby lanes

pois.name: Plaça de la Virreina
pois.why: Quiet square with a pretty church. Locals' favourite.
pois.kid: Listen for the church bell.
pois.tip: Sunset is around 18:45.
inside: Church of Sant Joan de Gràcia

pois.name: Tapeo Gràcia
pois.why: Neighbourhood tapas: ham croquettes, bombas, cod fritters.
pois.kid: Patatas bravas and croquetas are kid-proof.
pois.tip: Carrer Topazi 8. Check opening time; book if you can.

pois.name: Parc de la Creueta del Coll
pois.why: An old stone quarry turned into a park, with a huge concrete sculpture by Chillida hanging over the pond.
pois.kid: A giant stone claw hangs in the air on cables.
pois.tip: 15 min walk north of Park Güell.
inside: "Elogi de l'Aigua" by Chillida, a concrete sculpture hanging over the pond

pois.name: Jardins del Turó del Putxet
pois.why: Quiet hilltop park with a playground and a city view, mostly used by locals.
pois.kid: Playground at the top.
pois.tip: Good alternative if Park Güell's free zone is crowded.
inside: Hilltop park with a city view

pois.name: Parc del Guinardó
pois.why: Big wooded hill park just below the Bunkers, with paths and lookouts.
pois.kid: Forest paths in the middle of the city.
pois.tip: Pairs with the Bunkers on the way down.
inside: Wooded hill park with winding paths

pois.name: Plaça de la Revolució
pois.why: Long, sunny Gràcia square with a playground and ice cream shops.
pois.kid: Playground and ice cream in one stop.
pois.tip: Between Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Virreina.
inside: Long sunny square with plane trees

pois.name: CosmoCaixa science museum
pois.transitStop: FGC Av. Tibidabo (L7), then about 15 min on foot or bus V15 (check Maps)
pois.why: Hands-on science museum with a real flooded Amazon forest (piranhas, tropical fish, rain showers) and a giant Geological Wall.
pois.kid: Stay for the tropical rain that falls in the flooded forest every few hours.
pois.tip: Open daily 10:00–20:00. Planetarium seats are limited; book a session with your ticket. Café on site for lunch.
inside: Amazon Flooded Forest: a real wet-forest tank with fish, with a rain shower
Exhibitions on matter, life and space

pois.name: Arc de Triomf
pois.why: Red-brick arch built for the 1888 World Fair. Wide promenade for scooters and street music.
pois.kid: Race to the arch from the far end.
pois.tip: Metro L1 Arc de Triomf.
inside: Moorish-style red-brick arch from the 1888 World Fair

pois.name: Cascada fountain (Ciutadella)
pois.transitStop: Arc de Triomf (L1) or Ciutadella | Vila Olímpica (L4), 8 min
pois.why: A grand fountain with golden horses. Climb the stairs behind it.
pois.kid: A young Gaudí helped build this as a student.
pois.tip: Ciutadella Park has clean grass for a rest.
inside: Monumental fountain with a golden chariot
Stairs and terrace behind the fountain

pois.name: Ciutadella boating lake
pois.why: Rent a rowing boat for half an hour.
pois.kid: Let the child row. It's harder than it looks!
pois.tip: Boats may close early in autumn; check on the day.

pois.name: Mammoth statue
pois.why: A life-size stone mammoth from 1907. Barcelona's favourite photo with kids.
pois.kid: Stand by its tusk for scale.
pois.tip: Barcelona Zoo is next door (paid, optional).
inside: Zoo entrance next to the park

pois.name: Picasso Museum
pois.why: Picasso's early work, from childhood sketches to his blue period, in five medieval palaces.
pois.kid: Find drawings Picasso made when he was about your age.
pois.tip: Free Thursday afternoons and on the first Sunday of the month, with a timed booking. Arrive 10 min early.
inside: Early works: childhood sketches and academic paintings
Las Meninas series: Picasso's versions of Velázquez

pois.name: La Paradeta Born
pois.why: Pick your seafood at the counter, they cook it, you collect when your number is called.
pois.kid: Choosing the fish is part of the fun. Fried calamari is a safe bet.
pois.tip: Carrer Comercial 7. Queue forms early; go at opening.
inside: Pick fresh seafood at the counter
They cook it and call your number

pois.name: Umbracle & Hivernacle (Ciutadella)
pois.why: Two 19th-century iron-and-glass plant houses inside the park.
pois.kid: A shady house made of wooden slats for plants.
pois.tip: Near the park's Passeig de Picasso side.
inside: Umbracle: palm house with a wooden-slat roof

pois.name: Barcelona Zoo
pois.why: Big zoo inside Ciutadella Park, with a children's farm.
pois.kid: Elephants, gorillas and a petting farm.
pois.tip: Only if you skip CosmoCaixa or have a spare morning.

pois.name: Passeig de Sant Joan
pois.why: Wide boulevard with playgrounds every block, popular with local families.
pois.kid: Playground hopping up the avenue.
pois.tip: Watch for the bike lane in the middle.

pois.name: Jardins de la Tamarita
pois.why: Small leafy garden near CosmoCaixa with a play area, quiet and local.
pois.kid: A calm run-around after the museum.
pois.tip: 2 min from CosmoCaixa.
inside: Small garden with a play area

pois.name: Columbus Monument
pois.why: A 60 m column at the bottom of La Rambla.
pois.kid: Columbus is pointing at the Mediterranean, not at America.
pois.tip: Lion statues at the base are fine for photos.
inside: 60 m column with Columbus on top

pois.name: Rambla de Mar & Port Vell
pois.why: Wooden walkway over the harbour with yachts and sea views.
pois.kid: Watch the swing bridge if it opens for a boat.
pois.tip: The Aquarium is here if it rains.

pois.name: Mercat de la Barceloneta
pois.why: Modern neighbourhood market in the old fishermen's district.
pois.kid: Spot five kinds of fish you've never seen.
pois.tip: Buy fruit for the beach here.

pois.name: La Cova Fumada
pois.why: Tiny tavern where the 'bomba' (meat-and-potato ball with sauce) was invented.
pois.kid: One bomba each. Ask for less spicy sauce.
pois.tip: Cash only, weekday lunch, no sign outside. Arrive before 13:00.
inside: Bomba: potato and meat ball with spicy sauce
Fried sardines and artichokes in season

pois.name: L'Estel Ferit (stacked cubes)
pois.why: Rebecca Horn's rusty tower of cubes on the sand, a tribute to the old beach shacks.
pois.kid: Count the cubes.
pois.tip: Good meeting point if anyone gets lost.
inside: Tower of rusty stacked cubes by Rebecca Horn

pois.name: Barceloneta / Sant Miquel beach
pois.why: The city beach, a short walk from the old town.
pois.kid: Swim and dig. Stay where you can stand.
pois.tip: Lifeguards only in the summer season. Take turns watching the bags.
inside: Sea warm enough to swim from about June to October

pois.name: Peix d'Or (golden fish)
pois.why: Frank Gehry's giant copper fish from the 1992 Olympics.
pois.kid: Does it look like it's swimming or jumping?
pois.tip: Promenade is flat and great for walking.

pois.name: Bogatell beach
pois.why: Calmer family beach with a playground, ping-pong tables and outdoor gym.
pois.kid: Playground plus beach football.
pois.tip: Metro back: Llacuna (L4), 13 min walk.
inside: Playground, ping-pong tables and outdoor gym

pois.name: Parc de la Barceloneta
pois.why: Park around an old gasworks water tower, with a playground, next to the beach.
pois.kid: Playground break between swims.
pois.tip: Behind the beach near the hospital.
inside: Old water tower in the park

pois.name: Port Cable Car (Torre de Sant Sebastià)
pois.why: Old cable car crossing the harbour from Barceloneta to Montjuïc, 70 m above the water.
pois.kid: Fly over the ships in a hanging cabin.
pois.tip: Splurge option. One way takes you across the harbour to Montjuïc.

pois.name: Barceloneta breakwater (Rompeolas)
pois.why: Walk out along the sea wall at the tip of Barceloneta for open-sea views.
pois.kid: Waves splash against the big rocks.
pois.tip: Stay away from the edge on windy days.

pois.name: Rambla del Poblenou
pois.why: The locals' rambla: calm, tree-lined, with cafés and ice cream, a short walk inland from Bogatell.
pois.kid: Ice cream reward after the beach.
pois.tip: Metro Poblenou (L4) at the top end.

pois.name: Funicular de Montjuïc
pois.why: Underground funicular from Paral·lel metro up the hill.
pois.kid: It climbs like a train on a steep ramp.
pois.tip: From the top take bus 150 to the castle (T-casual). The cable car is the fun paid option: €17.10 adult / €11.70 child online.
inside: Underground funicular from Paral·lel to the Montjuïc park station
Connects to the cable car and bus 150

pois.name: Montjuïc Castle
pois.transitStop: Bus 150 from the funicular top station, or cable car plus 10 min walk
pois.why: Star-shaped fortress on top of the hill with views over the port and sea.
pois.kid: Walk around the moat and find the cannons.
pois.tip: The walls and views outside are free. Opening hours are shorter in winter.
inside: Star-shaped fortress with a dry moat
Walk along the walls with port views

pois.name: Mirador de l'Alcalde
pois.transitStop: Bus 150 or 55 | Paral·lel (L2, L3) plus funicular
pois.why: Terrace viewpoint over the harbour, paved with mosaic.
pois.kid: Wave at the cruise ships.
pois.tip: Downhill path from the castle.

pois.name: Jardins de Joan Brossa
pois.why: Old amusement-park grounds turned garden with play features.
pois.kid: Playground and space to roam. Good picnic stop.
pois.tip: Picnic lunch here; bring food from below.
inside: Gardens on a former amusement-park site

pois.name: Anella Olímpica
pois.why: The 1992 Olympic park with the white Calatrava tower.
pois.kid: Peek into the Olympic stadium gates.
pois.tip: Long, flat avenue. Toilets near the stadium.
inside: Palau Sant Jordi by Arata Isozaki

pois.name: MNAC museum & terrace
pois.costNote: Outside free · museum free Sat from 15:00
pois.why: Palace on the hill. The steps give the best view down to Plaça d'Espanya.
pois.kid: Count the steps down to the fountain.
pois.tip: Museum entry is free on Saturday afternoons and the first Sunday of the month.
inside: Wide steps with the view down to Plaça d'Espanya and the fountains

pois.name: Carrer de Blai (pintxos street)
pois.why: Pedestrian street of pintxo bars in Poble Sec. Locals' cheap night out.
pois.kid: Pick what looks good off the counter. Keep the sticks to pay.
pois.tip: Go early; it fills up after 20:00.

pois.name: Magic Fountain show
pois.why: Water, light and music show on the terraces below the MNAC.
pois.kid: The jets can shoot over 50 m high.
pois.tip: Show days and times change with the season and are cancelled in droughts: check the city's schedule on the day. Stand on the steps behind the fountain.
inside: Water, light and music show on the terraces
Steps behind the fountain for a full view

pois.name: Jardins de Mossèn Costa i Llobera
pois.why: Cactus garden on the sea-facing slope, with hundreds of species.
pois.kid: Find a cactus taller than a grown-up.
pois.tip: Below Mirador de l'Alcalde.

pois.name: Mirador del Migdia
pois.why: South-side viewpoint behind the castle, facing the open sea and the airport.
pois.kid: Count the planes landing.
pois.tip: Quieter than the castle; good at sunset.
inside: Viewpoint behind the castle facing open sea

pois.name: Jardins de Laribal & Font del Gat
pois.why: Terraced gardens with stairways, water channels and Moorish-style fountains.
pois.kid: Follow the little water channel down the steps.
pois.tip: On the way between the Anella and Poble Sec.

pois.name: Jardins de Mossèn Cinto Verdaguer
pois.why: Gardens with ponds of water lilies and bulb flowers, by the cable car station.
pois.kid: Look for frogs and fish in the ponds.
pois.tip: Right next to the funicular top station.

pois.name: Poble Espanyol
pois.why: Open-air village with copies of buildings from all over Spain and craft workshops.
pois.kid: Watch a glass-blower at work.
pois.tip: Optional; next to the Magic Fountain.
inside: Open-air village with copies of buildings from Spain

dayTrips.name: Montserrat
dayTrips.from: FGC Plaça d'Espanya, R5 towards Manresa, then rack railway or cable car
dayTrips.why: A jagged mountain 50 km from the city with a Benedictine monastery on the rock face. Go early: tour groups arrive around 11:00.
dayTrips.tip: Buy the combined train + rack railway or cable car ticket at fgc.cat or at the station. Check the last train down before lunch.

dayTrips.name: Girona
dayTrips.from: Barcelona Sants (fast Avant train ~40 min, or R11 regional ~1 h 20 min)
dayTrips.why: Coloured houses on the river, a walk on the medieval walls and a cathedral with a huge staircase.
dayTrips.tip: Book the fast Avant train a few days ahead on renfe.com. The R11 needs no booking.

dayTrips.name: Sitges
dayTrips.from: Barcelona Sants or Passeig de Gràcia, R2 Sud
dayTrips.why: A white seaside town with a church on the rocks, sandy beaches and a long promenade.
dayTrips.tip: Buy at the station machine; no booking needed. Many museums close on Mondays.
highlights: Passeig Marítim & Platja de la Ribera
Church of Sant Bartomeu and Santa Tecla

dayTrips.name: Tossa de Mar
dayTrips.why: A walled medieval village on a headland above a Costa Brava beach.
dayTrips.tip: Buy Sarfa tickets online and check the last bus back before you go.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: The T-casual card gives 10 rides in zone 1 on metro, bus, tram, FGC and local trains, with changes within 75 minutes. One card can be shared: validate once per person. Children aged 4 and over pay full fare. Google Maps shows live metro and bus times.

tips.title: Airport
tips.text: The R2 Nord train from Terminal 2 accepts the T-casual. The L9 airport metro needs a separate airport ticket. From T1, take the free shuttle bus to T2.

tips.title: Meal times
tips.text: Lunch 13:30–15:30, dinner from 20:30; many kitchens close in between. The weekday menú del día (three courses) is the best-value meal.

tips.title: Money
tips.text: Walk one street back from La Rambla and the seafront for normal prices. When paying by card, choose EUR. Tipping is optional; rounding up is enough. Tourist tax is paid per person per night, usually at the hotel.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Pickpockets work La Rambla, metro lines L1 and L3, Sagrada Família and the beaches. Wear bags in front and keep phones off café tables. Emergency number: 112.

tips.title: Book ahead
tips.text: Sagrada Família, Park Güell, Casa Batlló and Casa Milà sell timed tickets. Buy only on the official sites; resellers add a lot.
